Auditing Studies Across Several Servers

Source: vignettes/auditing-studies.Rmd
auditing-studies.Rmd

A federated study usually spans several DataSHIELD servers (sites). Both audit() and report() accept a named list of connections, one per site, and return one audit per element plus a combined report.

If you have not used audit() and report() before, start with vignette("getting-started", package = "dsROCrate").

library(dsROCrate)

1. Connect to each site

In a real study, each connection points to a different server. To keep this example self-contained, we open two connections to the same demo server and name them as if they were two sites. Use an administrator or Audit system account at every site.

USERNAME <- "administrator"
USERPASS <- "password"

cons <- list(
  site_a = opalr::opal.login(USERNAME, USERPASS, url = SERVER),
  site_b = opalr::opal.login(USERNAME, USERPASS, url = SERVER)
)

2. Audit the study

The arguments of audit() are applied to every site, so the project (and, if given, the user and tables) must exist in each of them.

study_audit <- cons |>
  audit(project = "CNSIM", tables = "CNSIM1", user = "dsuser")
#>  Found 333 records... Imported 333 records. Simplifying...
#>  Found 338 records... Imported 338 records. Simplifying...

# one RO-Crate per site
names(study_audit)
#> [1] "site_a" "site_b"

print(study_audit$site_a)

3. Create a study report

As for a single crate, we can first generate only the contents of the report:

report_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".Rmd")

study_parts <- study_audit |>
  report(filepath = report_file, render = FALSE)
